title: Hundreds Dead, Thousands More Missing After Catastrophic Flash Flood Hits Nepal-China Border
text:
Hundreds Dead, Thousands More Missing After Catastrophic Flash Flood Hits Nepal-China Border
Hundreds of tourists were caught in the path of the flood. Nepal's tourism authorities reported around 384 to over 400 people missing from the affected area
A massive flash flood and mudslide tore through the Himalayan border region between Nepal and China's Tibet Autonomous Region on Wednesday, August 26, 2026, killing at least 160 people and leaving hundreds missing, including large numbers of foreign tourists and pilgrims.
Nepal Police reported recovering 157 bodies across multiple districts, including Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Chitwan, Gorkha, Tanahun, and Nawalparasi. Chinese state media reported three confirmed deaths and 265 people missing in Gyirong County on the Tibetan side. The overall death toll stands at approximately 160, with the number of missing ranging from several hundred to over 750 in some early tallies as authorities continue searches.
The disaster struck early Wednesday morning near the Nepal-Tibet border, primarily affecting the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river systems. Preliminary assessments indicate an avalanche or rockslide-possibly linked to seismic activity or glacial instability-dammed a river before releasing a wall of water, mud, and debris that surged downstream. Dramatic surveillance footage from the Tibetan border crossing at Gyirong showed a sudden torrent engulfing buildings, vehicles, and people within seconds.
In Nepal, the floods washed away villages, bridges, roads, and hydropower infrastructure in districts north of Kathmandu. Entire riverside settlements were inundated, with some bodies recovered as far as 150 kilometers downstream. Dozens of Nepali security personnel, including police and army members, remain unaccounted for after their posts were swept away.
Hundreds of tourists were caught in the path of the flood. Nepal's tourism authorities reported around 384 to over 400 people missing from the affected area, the majority of them foreigners bound for the sacred Mount Kailash region in Tibet. Among the missing are more than 100 Indian nationals (many on the Kailash Mansarovar pilgrimage), dozens of Americans, Britons, Australians, Canadians, Malaysians, and citizens of other countries. Nepali nationals, including local trekkers and festival-goers, also number in the dozens among the missing.
Rescue operations involving the Nepali Army, police, and helicopters are underway on both sides of the border, complicated by washed-out roads, high water levels, and poor weather. Nepal's government ordered evacuations of vulnerable areas, while China has mobilized search teams. India has offered humanitarian assistance, and several countries are working to account for their nationals.
Authorities warn that the death toll is likely to rise as recovery efforts continue. The event ranks among Nepal's deadliest natural disasters in recent years and has heightened concerns about glacial outburst risks in the warming Himalayas.
Search and relief operations remain ongoing as of early Thursday. 98 people have been confirmed dead after catastrophic flash floods crashed through the China-Nepal border. 47 Americans missing (NYPost). 391 tourists missing. Flood may have been caused by a massive chunk of ice snapping off a glacier. "A chunk of ice with a width of about 2,000 feet snapped cleanly off the glacier... the chunk of ice fell from an altitude of around 17,000 feet, dropping almost 4,000 feet," the New York Times reported. 19 drive-able bridges have been destroyed.
